questions.q: What mindset does the book suggest adopting toward strangers' actions?
a: Assume they have good intentions unless proven otherwise
Assume they are always acting selfishly
Ignore their motives entirely
Judge them based on first impressions
questions.why: Lesson 1 advises assuming the best in people even when you have reasons not to.

questions.q: How does the author describe "failing productively"?
a: Viewing failure as a learning chance and analyzing mistakes
Avoiding failure by never taking risks
Celebrating failure without reflection
Blaming others for any setback
questions.why: Lesson 2 explains that treating failure as a lesson leads to productive outcomes.

questions.q: What does "trust the process" entail according to the book?
a: Believing consistent effort will eventually yield results
Expecting instant success after the first attempt
Relying on luck rather than planning
Skipping steps to speed up achievement
questions.why: Lesson 3 defines trusting the process as believing hard work pays off over time.

questions.q: Which concept explains why choosing one activity means losing another?
a: Opportunity cost
Marginal utility
Supply and demand
Economies of scale
questions.why: The overview introduces opportunity cost as the loss incurred when selecting one option over another.

questions.q: Why is patience highlighted as essential for long‑term goals?
a: Big objectives often need more time and repeated effort
Because quick wins are always better
Patience guarantees immediate results
It eliminates the need for planning
questions.why: Lesson 3 stresses that patient, incremental progress is the foundation of lasting success.
